content.text:
0.svg was empty: just `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"/>`, with no size and nothing drawn. With nothing to refine, I went by the filename and drew a "0":

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" role="img" aria-label="0">
  <path d="M12 3C15.9 3 18 6.15 18 12S15.9 21 12 21S6 17.85 6 12S8.1 3 12 3Z"/>
</svg>
```

- **Size:** It now uses a standard 24×24 icon canvas. Before, browsers would have shown it at their default size of 300×150.
- **Shape:** It's a slightly squared oval drawn as a path rather than text, so it looks the same whatever fonts are installed. It's narrower than a letter O so it reads as a digit. The sides, top and bottom line up with whole pixels at 24px, so they stay sharp.
- **Color:** `currentColor` makes it take on the surrounding text color when it's placed directly in an HTML page, and black anywhere else. The stroke settings are on the outer `<svg>` element, so CSS can change the line thickness.
- **Accessibility:** `role="img"` and `aria-label="0"` let screen readers announce it.

**Not checked:** Rendering a preview (resvg) and validating the XML (xmllint) both needed approval, which this session can't give. So I haven't seen how it actually looks; I only checked the markup and the curve coordinates by hand. I deleted the scratch file I used for comparing shapes, and the folder now holds only 0.svg.

If the file was meant to show something other than a zero, tell me what and I'll redo it.
